name: Forged by the Golden Melody
desc: A greatsword decorated in gold. Legend has it that it was the favored weapon of a certain exalted Harmost back in the distant past.

value.text:
Battle Pass - Gnostic Hymn
BP Bounty

Every 10s, the equipping character plays a "Harmonic Movement" of the corresponding type for a boost in the following order: + <color=#36ffff>18%/22.5%/27%/31.5%/36%</color> ATK > + <color=#36ffff>120/150/180/210/240</color> Elemental Mastery > + <color=#36ffff>28%/35%/42%/49%/56%</color> Stellar Glimmer reaction DMG. Each instance of Harmonic Movement lasts 10s. This effect can trigger even when the equipping character is not on the field.
Triggering a Stellar Glimmer reaction will also grant an additional 12-second instance of "Harmonic Movement: Contrapuntal" with the same effects as the Harmonic Movement active when Stellar Glimmer is triggered. This effect stacks with the original Harmonic Movement effect, and can trigger once every 12s.

materials.name: Dross of Pure Sacred Dewdrop
materials.desc:
Legends say that before the birth of life, there was a dense primordial sea. It is the purest origin of all things, and one day, it will also swallow all life... and those things which did not arise from it will be filtered out, becoming naught but floating detritus.

"The existence of detritus also has meaning — What kind of thing would be rejected by the source of all things that swallows all life?" the young Harmost asked the great usurper, pondering this conundrum.

materials.desc:
A stone hilt obtained from an ancient statue.

Its luster has long been lost to the depredations of seawater.

materials.name: Transoceanic Pearl
materials.desc:
A small crystal obtained from a defeated Fontemer Aberrant.

Fontemer Aberrants arise from Fontaine's sea. They are believed to be a unique life form born from the mysterious energy in the water.

materials.name: Sublimation of Pure Sacred Dewdrop
materials.desc:
"Life that came from the primordial sea is inevitably fated to return to it." Thus spoke the Harmost Boethius. "But there are infinite possibilities for humans to transcend, and even the waters of the primordial sea cannot completely dissolve them..."

The arrogant usurper once attempted to mix insoluble Ichor with pure water, to contain wisdom and memories, allowing his subjects and servants to discard their physical bodies, and obtain independent, eternal lives.

But the pain of severing soul and body cannot be endured by any ordinary life, and the usurper's order tore apart and shattered souls...

The Ichor was dyed black by the crying and howling of so many souls, and it lost its harmony and wisdom, leaving only chaos and madness.

It gives off a somewhat mysterious energy. Although many legends speak of great life forms residing in remote seas beyond human reach, ordinary oceans can hardly compare to the vibrant seas of Fontaine.

materials.name: Spring of Pure Sacred Dewdrop
materials.desc: This is a relic from a time when the Lochknights still roamed — the knights said, there were still loyal spirits in the mountain springs and valleys where none tread, guarding those pure, unpolluted springs... However, the creator of artificial Ichor couldn't tolerate any discord in his great symphony. It is said that wherever the Harmost Boethius went, the natural nectar was buried, the aqueducts of the empire were built, and the spirits born of pure water vanished without a trace...

materials.name: Essence of Pure Sacred Dewdrop
materials.desc:
A dense and pure solution, derived and refined from drops of the vast primordial sea. The ancient God King once believed it would bring eternal life and infinite wisdom, but listening carefully — it was quietly, faintly prophesizing the final end of all dissolving into one. This was once the God King's unfinished Grand Symphony — a boundless, sourceless golden Ichor replacing the wild primeval waters, and the glorious immortal sages bringing nectar-like enlightenment to the ignorant corners of the world.

But the God King's delusions ultimately sank into the depths of the black abyss, and with the ravages of time, the golden Ichor was eventually corroded by the primordial soup...

The tuner turned a blind eye to the evil omens, and supporting his broken body, continued to give life to his compatriots according to the plans once laid, so that the old order might one day return...

Even today, many mad poets and painters of Fontaine see the apocalypse experienced by Boethius, a reminder of the inescapable cycle of the world.

desc.text:
In silent corridors made from white stone, the sacred law of eternal harmony held leisurely sway between the musicians' fingers.
The golden-haired bosom friend caressed the magnificent purple robe, then bent to whisper in the musician's ear.
"My friend. My brother. Lift your head and look at those benighted slaves."
Though the voice was sweet as honey and gentle as a song, it was filled with unmistakable pride.
"The foolishness of this rabble, to take the grueling toil we bear for decadent lives of luxury."
"A shame, a shame indeed... that this beautiful solo should fall upon mortal sod."
The musician stopped playing and spoke no refutation, simply sighing.
Indeed, though it could cause the very bones of the earth to shake and make miracles mortals could not fathom,
The duty known as attunement, of cleansing the bitter sorrow of all waters, was essentially to burn one's soul like firewood.
The sorrow, the pain, and the resentment that flowed through the high canals had to be harmonized and purified by them,
Such that the God King in his golden palace could fulfill his great, tragic wish to save all souls.
"Do not let pride and arrogance blind you, my friend, my brother."
"We were elevated to guide and rescue those foolish slaves you speak of."
"How shall we play the Sebastos' perfect melody, if we despise them so?"
His golden-haired friend snorted coldly and rebuked him bitterly for his weakness. Then, he sat down beside him and began playing on the strings of his lyre.
His thought should have been perfected, and yet, as the strings echoed, what he saw were afterimages of his past.
Once, he too was a foolish person of bygone times, holding onto what he now knew to be weak expectation,
Yet, the watery moonlight and tender, lingering whispers ultimately faded amidst the clamoring bugles, leaving behind only solemn vows unfulfilled.
Perhaps he should not have become a Harmost, he thought, for he had never possessed such lofty delusions,
But instead, continued to imagine, even as he had in the past, that the descendants of those who dwelled on the high sea might suffer less.
"She never believed in the gods, for those who believe in gods would never commit atrocities in their name."
That was how his female companion, kind and loving as an elder sister, had once lamented the untrustworthiness of the barbarian tribes.
Yes, he thought, of course she would not believe in the gods. But had he not been the same way regarding the Sebastos of the golden palace?
Had she been the one to ascend, she too would have bowed before the Sebastos.
If he had been the one determined to take revenge, he would surely have falsely claimed to come in a god's name.
The musician, the proud musician, the musician who claimed humility, always believed that.
He believed that just as he could read her thoughts, he could also read the unspoken sorrows within the people's hearts.
Thus did much time pass, until that rebellious fantasy dissipated in the light,
Until the grievances of the past were utterly erased, when countless scattered wills finally gained restful slumber within the waterways,
Until, at the final moment, when he gazed upon the golden-haired traveler — only then did the musician understand...
That none can claim to understand another's heart until the final hour arrives.
It was not just her. His dear friend's fanaticism, his female companion's compassion, his God King's grand design...
He could not say that he had fully understood a single one of them.
Perhaps all the musical passages in this world were but fragments that could never play together,
And those who float or sink upon the high sea did nothing in the end but echo within their solitude.
But that was no longer important. It was all water under the bridge.
All dreams, noble, despicable, pure, filthy,
They all converged into the waters like lightly falling raindrops,
Like the tears she had shed while embracing his broken body,
Silently disappearing into the shadows of the symphony of night and day.

customize.name: Heretic's Molten Blade
customize.desc: He drew this weapon once more when he first met that God of Flame, revered by all, but it had been too long since he had last used it.

customize.desc: A spear of solid ice imbued with an icy chill. It is said that it once belonged to the Belyi Tsar who ruled Snezhnaya in the distant past.

customize.name: Clash of Kings
customize.desc: A golden box lavishly inlaid with precious jewels. It houses a game much beloved by the kings of the sands.

customize.desc: A longbow of immense strength. It shines with the radiance of dreams even in the darkest of nights.
